idiom_name: http4s HttpRoutes (or akka-http routing DSL) with circe codecs as the published shapes
implementation_notes: Scala publishes the protocol as declared routes - http4s HttpRoutes.of { case req @ POST -> Root / "v1" / "orders" => ... } or akka-http's pathPrefix("v1") block - where the circe (or µPickle) codecs define the wire shapes and therefore the contract, and a DTO case class carrying only published fields is the translation layer. The version lives in the path or in an Accept media type, and where tapir-style endpoint descriptions are used the same declarations generate the OpenAPI document, keeping the document and the implementation from drifting. Implicit codec derivation is the trap in this language: the moment a codec instance exists for a domain type, that type is published.
pitfalls: A codec instance on a domain case class publishes it: adding or renaming a field then changes the wire contract, so keep encoders on DTOs.
Implicit derivation silently publishes every field of a case class, including ones added for internal reasons later.
Blocking side effects (JDBC, file IO) evaluated on the wrong execution context starve the runtime - keep them on a dedicated blocking pool.
